pages.name: A stretch of answers
pages.text: An [[inequality]] such as `x > 3` says `x` is greater than 3, so it has many answers: 4 works, 3.5 works, but 3 does not. They make a stretch of the number line, with an open circle because 3 is left out and an arrow because it carries on for ever. Drag the marker to try any number.

pages.name: Less than or equal
pages.task: `≤` means [[less than or equal to]], so `x ≤ 2` includes 2 itself, and `≥` means [[greater than or equal to]]. Which picture shows `x ≤ 2`?
pages.why: `x ≤ 2` includes 2, so its circle is filled, and every number below 2 works too, so the stretch runs left. Put back 0 and 2: `0 ≤ 2` and `2 ≤ 2` are both true.

pages.name: Same undo moves
pages.text: You solve an inequality with the same undo moves as an equation, doing each one to both sides. Try `x = 5`: taking 3 from both sides slides both dots along, and halving both squeezes them towards 0 without crossing it. Half of the bigger distance is still the bigger one, so the bigger side stays on the right. That leaves `x > 4`.

pages.why: Divide both sides by 3 to get `x − 2 ≥ 4`, then add 2 to both sides to get `x ≥ 6`. Put back 6 and it makes 12; put back 7 and it makes 15. Both are at least 12, so 6 gets a filled circle.

pages.name: A negative flips it
pages.text: Take something true, `10 < 15`, and multiply both sides by −5: each number mirrors across 0, to −10 and −15, then stretches five times as far, to −50 and −75. 15 was further right, but now it is further left, so `−50 > −75` and the sign flips. Multiplying or dividing both sides by a [[negative number]] reverses the sign, while a positive number keeps it.

pages.name: Dividing by a negative
pages.why: Divide both sides by −4, a negative number, so the sign flips: `x ≤ −5`. Put back −5 and it makes 20; put back −6 and it makes 24. Both are at least 20.

pages.name: Two routes
pages.text: You can even dodge the negative. Solve `7 − 3x ≥ 1` by dividing by −3 and flipping, or by adding `3x` to both sides first so nothing is divided by a negative. Both give `x ≤ 2`, because `2 ≥ x` read from the other end says the same thing.

pages.name: Mixed: loads on a circuit
pages.task: The circuit has a 20 A limit and already carries a 6 A heater, and each extra load draws 2 A, so `x` loads make `6 + 2x` amps. How many loads keep `6 + 2x ≤ 20`?
pages.why: Take 6 from both sides to get `2x ≤ 14`, then divide both sides by 2: `x ≤ 7`. Loads come whole, so it is 0 to 7 of them: 7 make 20 A, right on the limit, and 8 would make 22 A.
